narrative:
The model estimates a 58% chance that you will leave your current role, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that, in combination, signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues who are expected to stay.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at the company. Most employees who are predicted to stay (77%) report receiving no such offers, so this factor pushes the prediction noticeably toward leaving.

The second most important factor is your overall career experience of more than 11 years. While this is valuable, only 15% of employees expected to stay have this level of total experience. The model sees longer-tenured professionals as more likely to explore external options, so this also pulls the outcome toward leaving.

Third, you find balancing work and personal life difficult. Only 9% of colleagues predicted to stay report the same struggle. This challenge further increases the model’s estimate that you may choose to depart.

Taken together, these three elements outweigh many positive aspects of your profile, such as high job satisfaction, strong recognition, and good emotional commitment. The organization should discuss ways to reduce work-life pressure and explore retention options with you. You may wish to reflect on whether the external opportunities better match your long-term goals.
